text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: DNS resolution error rate spike detected for api.redwood.com (edge egress) — 5xx upstreams increasing in eu-west-1. Automated probes show ~12% DNS timeout/NXDOMAIN from global resolvers in the last 5m. Runbook: https://runbook.internal/dns-geo-failures (reacted :eyes:).

oncall-jamie: Ack. I'm on it. Paging net-eng and SRE. Logging incident channel + creating short incident page.

net-eng-lee: Looking at authoritative answers — Cloudflare geo DNS is returning older region IPs for several EU prefixes while Route53 returns the updated set. Some resolvers are getting mixed answers depending on nearest CF POP. Could be Cloudflare propagation lag + stale cache on some resolvers. Examples from probes:
```
; dig +short api.redwood.com @1.1.1.1 -> 52.14.200.11
; dig +short api.redwood.com @8.8.8.8 -> 52.14.200.11
; dig +short api.redwood.com @ns1.cloudflare.com -> 54.72.100.9
; dig +short api.redwood.com @ns-aws-route53 -> 52.14.200.11
```
CF authoritative sometimes returns 54.72.100.9 (old origin) which is currently drained and returning 502s.

sre-ash: We're seeing customer 5xx alerts tied to that IP. Canary telemetry shows error fraction spikes from EU customers hitting 54.72.100.9. Correlating with DNS TTLs — we recently changed origin pool and reduced weight for that IP but TTL was 300. Some resolvers not honoring TTLs or returning cached CF answers.

support-kim: Multiple premium customers reporting intermittent failures; one large customer in DE reported 30+ API timeouts in the last 10 mins. They're asking for ETA and mitigation.

oncall-jamie: Summary for execs: DNS divergence between Cloudflare and Route53 causing some EU resolvers to return an old origin IP that's draining and 502ing. Impact: intermittent 5xx for EU customers, some timeouts. Currently investigating mitigation.

net-eng-lee: Mitigation options: 1) Force Cloudflare to invalidate/flush zone (purge) / request expedited propagation via CF support. 2) Change GeoDNS preference to Route53 for EU (flip fallback). 3) Short-term announce traffic steering by updating Cloudflare Worker/edge redirect to prefer new origin IPs. 4) Increase weight on healthy origins and remove drained IP from DNS.

sre-ash: Doing quick cost/impact check — changing Route53 preference likely fastest to reduce failures but requires updating traffic policies and waiting for TTLs. Purge on CF is quicker if CF accepts and propagates.

oncall-jamie: Action plan (short):
- net-eng-lee: attempt CF zone purge + open high-priority ticket (CF SLA).
- net-eng-lee + sre-ash: prepare and test Route53 failover policy flip (dry-run), ready to apply if CF purge doesn't converge in 10m.
- devops-bot: start broad probe sweep across public resolvers every 30s and attach logs here.
- support-kim + pm-ana: draft customer-facing note for impacted customers and status page update.

net-eng-lee: CF purge initiated and support ticket opened (case #CF-2024-9087). CF purge returned 202 accepted. Pushing probe results...

devops-bot: Probe batch 1 results (timestamped): 1m ago -> 14% resolvers still returning old IP 54.72.100.9, 6m ago -> 38%. Trend improving.

pm-ana: Quick Q for SRE: any risk in flipping Route53 to preferred for EU? will it create split-brain with CF?

sre-ash: Minimal risk — Route53 already authoritative for fallback. We'll update traffic policy to prefer Route53 geo responses for EU only (scoped), leave other regions untouched. We'll schedule the change, monitor, and be ready to revert. I recommend a partial rollout (canary to 20% of queries).

support-kim: Sending preliminary message to affected customers: "We're investigating reports of intermittent API failures in EU. Root cause appears to be DNS propagation inconsistencies between Cloudflare and our Route53 configuration. We're actively applying mitigations and will update within 30 minutes." (sent)

oncall-jamie: Proceed with CF purge + 10m wait. If >10% of resolvers still returning old IPs, execute Route53 preference canary. Keep me posted every 5m.

net-eng-lee: CF purge + ticket didn't fully converge; at +8m probes still show ~9% of resolvers returning 54.72.100.9. Preparing Route53 policy change now. Pushing the canary to 20% EU resolvers (manual config).

devops-bot: Probe batch 5 => old-ip fraction down to 4%. Latency on those failed calls is high and error types = 502/504.

sre-ash: Canary applied. Early telemetry: error rate for canary group dropped from 5.2% -> 0.8% in last 2m. Increasing canary to 60%.

pm-ana: Need a short status blurb for customers: "Mitigation in progress — we're steering EU traffic away from stale origin IPs and errors are decreasing. If you're still seeing errors, please DM support and include request IDs."

support-kim: Status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1748881234 (initial note + mitigation).

oncall-jamie: Good. Let's keep canary ramp until 100% if metrics continue to improve. After ramp, follow-up actions: request CF confirm full purge, set TTL to 60s for next 24h, and run a postmortem on DNS change procedure to avoid future leftover IPs.

net-eng-lee: Canary at 100%. All probes now returning new origin IP set. CF confirmed propagation in ticket reply: "Purge complete, propagation observed at most POPs." Closing CF ticket.

sre-ash: Error rates back to baseline. Rolling TTL change to 60s for next 24h and adding an automation to remove drained origins from geo-answers immediately upon drain event.

oncall-jamie: Incident resolved -> impact: intermittent EU 5xxs for ~25 minutes, root cause: Cloudflare geo-authoritative propagation of stale zone data combined with drained origin IP still present in CF answers. Actions: CF purge, Route53 canary flip, TTL reduction, automation for origin removal, customer comms.

pm-ana: I'll own the postmortem and customer follow-up. ETA for postmortem draft: 48h.

support-kim: Notified affected customers with follow-up note and offered credits where appropriate.

oncall-jamie: Handoff to night oncall (oncall-maya) in 30m. Summary posted to #incidents and to pager duty incident. If anything resurfaces raise to P1 and page core triage.

oncall-maya: Ack and taking over at 18:30 UTC. Thanks all. (reacted :thumbsup:)

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED at 1748881289 — monitoring mode. Metrics indicate stable traffic and no ongoing DNS divergences.
